records.Concise description: Digital Matter Theory token conventions that derive supply or traits from deterministic Bitcoin block-data patterns.
records.Deeper researched summary: NATs operationalize DMT by tying token issuance or properties to discoverable patterns in Bitcoin data instead of arbitrary issuer-selected scarcity. The ecosystem later developed hybrid and UNAT models that can combine deterministic supply with inscription-based art or metadata. NAT interpretation requires compatible indexing software and should be presented as a metaprotocol convention rather than native Bitcoin token state.
Creators / founders: DMT ecosystem / The Block Runner — framework origin
records.Launch / history: Developed as a DMT implementation layer during 2023–2024 and continued evolving through later NAT/UNAT standards.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: NATs are the principal asset model that turned DMT theory into collectible and fungible experiments, including Natcats and other block-data-native projects.
Research notes / uncertainties: MSC should avoid presenting NAT supply/state as Bitcoin consensus-enforced.

records.Concise description: An Ordinals-based metaprotocol that extends BRC-20-style assets with additional transfer, trading, authority, DMT, and Bitmap-oriented capabilities.
records.Deeper researched summary: TAP is an inscription metaprotocol designed to retain compatibility with familiar BRC-20 concepts while adding features such as mass-send, peer-to-peer trading mechanics, token authorities, and integrations with DMT/Bitmap concepts. Its state is interpreted by TAP-compatible indexers. It is best represented as a programmable metaprotocol layer rather than as a native Bitcoin protocol feature.
Creators / founders: Trac/TAP project team — official documentation verified; individual founder attribution not locked from first-party sources
records.Launch / history: Developed after BRC-20 during the 2023–2024 Ordinals metaprotocol expansion and remains documented in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: TAP illustrates the move from simple inscription-token experiments toward richer programmable asset behavior on Ordinals-aware indexers.
Research notes / uncertainties: Individual founders require first-party confirmation before a public creator field is expanded.

records.Concise description: A collector-defined cohort of inscriptions with numbers below 1,000, valued primarily for extreme early placement in Ordinals history.
records.Deeper researched summary: Sub-1k is not a coordinated collection. It is a retrospective historical cohort used by collectors and marketplaces to group very early numbered inscriptions. Membership depends on inscription-number conventions and indexing history, so MSC should treat the label as an ecosystem index rather than a project. The cohort contains work from multiple creators and experiments from Ordinals’ first days.
Creators / founders: No single creator — cross-project historical cohort
records.Launch / history: The inscriptions themselves date to the first phase of Ordinals in early 2023; the 'Sub-1k' category emerged as collectors organized historical inscription ranges.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: Sub-1k captures the earliest publicly indexed experimentation and is a key provenance/chronology lens for Ordinals collecting.
records.Verification basis: Indexer/market cohort usage plus independent historical chronology.
Research notes / uncertainties: This is a collector/indexing category, not an official project.
Inscription numbering can be affected by historical indexing conventions; avoid implying consensus significance.

records.Concise description: A collector-defined cohort covering the first roughly ten thousand numbered Ordinals inscriptions.
records.Deeper researched summary: Sub-10k is a retrospective historical category rather than one collection. It is widely used to discuss the formative January–February 2023 inscription era, and it overlaps with early art projects, experiments, PFPs, and one-offs. Some community/index definitions differ on whether inscription #10,000 is included; MSC should present the boundary as a convention, not a protocol rule.
Creators / founders: No single creator — cross-project historical cohort
records.Launch / history: Covers the earliest Ordinals inscription period in 2023; the label became a common collector/indexing shorthand.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: The cohort provides a useful historical map of the ecosystem before large coordinated 10k collections became common.
records.Verification basis: Independent historical chronology and current indexer usage.
Research notes / uncertainties: Some ecosystem treatments include #10,000 while the literal mathematical boundary is <10,000; retain wording 'roughly first ten thousand' in public copy.
